definition: In this psychology context, vicarious means felt indirectly through another person or group rather than from one’s own actions. For example, a person may experience shame because of misconduct by members of their own group.

reasons: The packet supports the specific phrase “vicarious shame” in sport spectatorship, not a general definition of “vicarious” as an indirect feeling across psychology contexts.
